title: Quick sauce 1: roasted tomato & feta
desc: The sauce you make in the dish you roasted in: burst cherry tomatoes, soft garlic and feta mashed into the oily juice. No pan, no packet. This is the sauce from the broccoli-chicken bake.
reheat: Gently in a pan with a splash of water.
left: Stir into eggs or spoon over any grilled chicken.
trouble: Mash longer and add 1 tbsp hot water or cream; feta melts into the juice when it is warm.
Feta is salty: add no salt until you have tasted the finished sauce.
Mash in more feta or a few more tomatoes; oil and juice need something to hold on to.
Cherry tomatoes give little juice: next time use 2 big ripe tomatoes cut in chunks (same weight) for a looser, bigger sauce.
goes: Chicken, white fish, roasted vegetables, pasta.

steps.t: Put the chicken, whole cherry tomatoes and whole garlic cloves in the air-fryer dish, pour over the olive oil, sprinkle the basil and pepper. Put the feta block on top. Air-fry at 190 °C for 20 minutes.
steps.w: The heat bursts the tomatoes and softens the garlic and feta; that is the raw material of the sauce.
steps.c: Tomatoes wrinkled and split, feta golden at the edges.
steps.m: Cutting the tomatoes first: whole ones keep their juice until they burst.
steps.img: air fryer dish with burst cherry tomatoes, garlic cloves and golden feta block next to chicken

steps.t: Lift the chicken onto the plate. Leave everything else in the dish. With a fork, press every tomato flat until it bursts, press every garlic clove flat, then mash the feta into the juice.
steps.w: Burst tomato juice + melted feta + garlic oil is the whole sauce; the fork is your blender.
steps.c: No whole tomatoes or cloves left, the feta is broken into the juice.
steps.m: Lifting the tomatoes out with the chicken: they belong in the sauce.
steps.img: fork pressing burst cherry tomatoes and feta into oily juice in a dish

steps.t: Stir hard for 30 seconds until it turns into a thick, pinkish sauce. Too thick: stir in 1 to 2 tbsp cream or hot water. Taste, add pepper, then spoon it over the chicken.
steps.w: Stirring hard joins the oil and the juice into one creamy sauce (an emulsion).
steps.c: Creamy, pink, coats the back of a spoon.
steps.m: Adding salt before tasting: the feta already brings plenty.
steps.img: creamy pink tomato feta sauce spooned over chicken breast

title: Quick sauce 2: pan juices & cream
desc: After frying meat, the brown bits stuck to the pan are pure flavour. Loosen them with water, add cream, let it bubble. The basic move behind most restaurant sauces.
reheat: Gently, with a splash of water.
trouble: Pan was too hot; black bits taste bitter, so wipe them out and start the sauce with butter and a little stock instead.
Let it bubble 1 to 2 minutes longer; it thickens as the water cooks off.
Stir in a splash of water off the heat.
goes: Chicken, pork, steak, with rice or vegetables.

steps.t: Salt and pepper the chicken. Fry in the oil on medium-high until cooked through, then put it on a plate. Do NOT wash the pan.
steps.w: The brown layer stuck to the pan (fond) is the flavour base of the sauce.
steps.c: Brown, sticky patches on the bottom of the pan, not black.
steps.m: Washing or wiping the pan now: you throw away the sauce.
steps.img: empty frying pan with brown caramelised bits after frying chicken

steps.t: Turn the heat to medium. Add the garlic for 30 seconds, then pour in the water. Scrape the bottom of the pan with a wooden spoon until all the brown bits come loose and the water turns brown.
steps.w: Water dissolves the stuck-on flavour; this is called deglazing.
steps.c: Pan bottom clean, liquid light brown.
steps.m: Not scraping: the flavour stays stuck to the pan.
steps.img: wooden spoon scraping brown bits from pan bottom into water

steps.t: Pour in the cream and let it bubble on medium for 2 to 3 minutes, stirring, until it is thick enough to coat the spoon. Pour in any juice from the chicken plate, taste, salt, spoon over the chicken.
steps.w: Bubbling cooks the water off, so the sauce thickens by itself.
steps.c: Draw a finger across the back of the spoon: the line stays.
steps.m: Serving it after 30 seconds: it is still watery.
steps.img: light brown cream sauce bubbling in a frying pan, coating a wooden spoon

title: Quick sauce 3: mustard cream
desc: Quick sauce 2 plus a spoon of Dijon. Sharp, creamy, ready in 3 minutes. Works with chicken, pork and salmon.
reheat: Gently, with a splash of water.
trouble: Mustard went in on high heat: take the pan off the heat and whisk in 1 tbsp water.
goes: Chicken, pork chops, salmon, green beans.

steps.t: Salt the chicken and fry it in the oil until cooked through. Put it on a plate; keep the unwashed pan.
steps.w: Same start as quick sauce 2: the brown bits are the base.
steps.c: Brown patches in the pan.
steps.m: Wiping the pan.
steps.img: browned chicken breasts resting on a plate next to a frying pan

steps.t: Medium heat: pour in the water and scrape the brown bits loose with a wooden spoon. Add the cream and let it bubble 2 minutes.
steps.w: Deglaze, then reduce: the two moves of every pan sauce.
steps.c: Slightly thickened, light brown.
steps.m: Skipping the scraping.
steps.img: cream bubbling in a frying pan

steps.t: Turn the heat to low and stir in the mustard until smooth. Taste, add pepper, then spoon over the chicken.
steps.w: Mustard added on low heat stays smooth and keeps its bite.
steps.c: Pale yellow, smooth, coats the spoon.
steps.m: Boiling it hard after the mustard: it can turn grainy.
steps.img: smooth pale yellow mustard cream sauce in a pan

title: Quick sauce 4: lemon butter
desc: Pan juices, a squeeze of lemon and cold butter swirled in off the heat. Glossy and fresh, no cream needed.
reheat: Not great reheated; make it fresh.
trouble: Pan was too hot: take it off the heat first, then swirl the butter in.
Swirl in a little more butter.
goes: Chicken, fish, salmon, broccoli, green beans.

steps.t: Salt the chicken and fry it in the oil until cooked through. Plate it; keep the pan.
steps.w: The brown bits are the base again.
steps.c: Brown patches in the pan.
steps.m: Wiping the pan.
steps.img: chicken breasts resting next to a frying pan with brown bits

steps.t: Medium heat: garlic for 30 seconds, then the water. Scrape the brown bits loose and let it bubble until about half is left (1 to 2 minutes). Add the lemon juice.
steps.w: Reducing first makes the sauce taste strong instead of watery.
steps.c: About 3 tablespoons of brown liquid left in the pan.
steps.m: Adding the butter while there is still a lot of water: the sauce stays thin.
steps.img: small amount of brown pan juice reducing in a frying pan

steps.t: Take the pan OFF the heat. Add the cold butter cubes and swirl the pan in circles until they melt into a glossy sauce. Pepper, then spoon over the chicken.
steps.w: Cold butter melted off the heat stays creamy; on the heat it splits into fat.
steps.c: Shiny, slightly thick, no pool of yellow fat.
steps.m: Leaving the pan on the flame while the butter melts.
steps.img: glossy lemon butter sauce swirling in a frying pan

title: Quick sauce 5: garlic yogurt (cold)
desc: No cooking at all: thick yogurt, grated garlic, lemon, salt, olive oil. The cold sauce for anything grilled or spicy.
trouble: Use thick Greek yogurt; thin yogurt can drain in a sieve for 20 minutes.
Let it stand 15 minutes; next time use half a clove.
goes: Grilled chicken, souvlaki, burgers, spicy food, roasted vegetables.

steps.t: Grate the garlic very fine. Stir it into the yogurt with the lemon juice and salt.
steps.w: Grated garlic spreads through the yogurt; chopped garlic gives raw chunks.
steps.c: Smooth, thick, white.
steps.m: Using a whole big clove: raw garlic gets stronger as it sits.
steps.img: bowl of thick white garlic yogurt sauce

steps.t: Drizzle the olive oil on top, taste, add salt if needed. Leave it 10 minutes in the fridge while you cook, then serve cold next to the hot food.
steps.w: Ten minutes lets the garlic and lemon soften into the yogurt.
steps.c: Thick enough to sit on a spoon without running off.
steps.m: Spooning it into a hot pan: yogurt splits when heated.
steps.img: garlic yogurt sauce drizzled with olive oil next to grilled chicken

title: Quick sauce 6: 5-minute tomato paste sauce
desc: Fry a spoon of tomato paste in the pan fat until it darkens, loosen it with water, season. A red sauce in 5 minutes from things that keep for months.
reheat: In a pan with a splash of water.
trouble: The paste was not fried long enough: fry it until it turns from bright red to brick red.
More water, a splash at a time.
A splash of cream or a knob of butter rounds it off (no sugar).

steps.t: Salt the chicken thighs and fry in the oil until cooked through. Plate them; keep the pan with its fat.
steps.w: The fat and brown bits carry the flavour into the tomato paste.
steps.c: Brown bits and a little fat in the pan.
steps.m: Pouring the fat away: the paste needs it to fry in.
steps.img: fried chicken thighs on a plate next to pan with fat

steps.t: Medium heat: garlic for 30 seconds, then the tomato paste and paprika. Stir and fry the paste for 1 to 2 minutes until it turns from bright red to darker brick red.
steps.w: Frying the paste cooks out the raw, tinny taste and makes it sweet and deep.
steps.c: Darker red, smells sweet, starts sticking a little.
steps.m: Adding the water straight away: the sauce tastes raw.
steps.img: tomato paste frying in a pan, darkening to brick red

steps.t: Pour in the water and scrape the pan, stirring until the paste dissolves into a smooth red sauce. Let it bubble 2 minutes, taste, salt, add chilli if you like, and put the chicken back in to coat.
steps.w: Water turns the fried paste into a sauce; bubbling thickens it.
steps.c: Smooth, glossy red, coats the chicken.
steps.m: Too much water at once: add it in two goes.
steps.img: chicken thighs coated in glossy red tomato sauce in a pan

title: Quick sauce 7: garlic confit with parmesan
desc: Whole garlic cloves cooked slowly in oil until soft and sweet, then mashed with butter, chilli, parmesan and a splash of water into a glossy sauce. The pan way to soft garlic. Served over chicken and green beans instead of pasta.
reheat: Gently in a pan with a spoon of water; do not boil or the cheese goes stringy.
left: Spare soft cloves keep 3 days in the fridge covered in their oil: mash one into eggs, dressings or any pan sauce.
trouble: The heat was too high or the time too short. Keep the oil barely bubbling and give them 5 more minutes: a fork must go through with no push.
Too hot. They should turn pale gold, never brown. Next time lower the heat and turn them more often.
Add another spoon of water off the heat and stir hard: water and cheese pull the oil into the sauce.
The pan was too hot. Take it off the heat before the parmesan goes in.
goes: Chicken, white fish, green beans, broccoli; a small portion of wholegrain pasta.

steps.t: Put the peeled whole garlic cloves and the olive oil in a small saucepan on LOW heat. Let them bubble very gently for 15 to 20 minutes, turning them now and then.
steps.w: Slow heat in oil cooks garlic through until it is soft and sweet instead of sharp. This is the pan route to garlic you can mash.
steps.c: Pale gold all over and a fork goes through with no push.
steps.m: Medium heat: they brown outside and stay hard inside.
steps.img: whole garlic cloves gently bubbling in olive oil in a small saucepan

steps.t: While the garlic cooks, salt and pepper the chicken and fry it in a spoon of the garlic oil in the frying pan, 5 minutes a side. Boil the green beans in salted water for 5 minutes and drain.
steps.w: The garlic oil already flavours the chicken; everything is ready at the same time.
steps.c: Chicken golden and firm, beans bright green with a little bite.
steps.m: Moving the chicken so it cannot brown.
steps.img: chicken breasts browning in a frying pan, green beans in a pot

steps.t: Make the sauce: lift the chicken onto the plates. Turn the heat to low and tip the soft cloves and their oil into the chicken pan with the butter and chilli flakes. Mash half the cloves with a fork, pour in the water and scrape the bottom of the pan. Take the pan off the heat, add the parmesan and stir hard for 30 seconds until it turns into a glossy, creamy sauce. Stir in the parsley.
steps.w: Water and cheese pull the oil and butter together into a sauce; off the heat the cheese melts smoothly instead of going stringy.
steps.c: Glossy and creamy, coats the back of the spoon, no pool of oil around the edge.
steps.m: Adding the cheese on the heat: it clumps.
steps.img: glossy garlic parmesan sauce with soft garlic cloves in a frying pan

steps.t: Turn the green beans through the sauce, plate them next to the chicken and spoon the rest of the sauce and whole cloves over. A squeeze of lemon on top.
steps.w: Lemon cuts the richness of butter and cheese.
steps.c: Every bean shiny with sauce.
steps.m: Leaving the sauce in the pan.
steps.img: chicken with green beans and garlic parmesan sauce on a plate
